newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban chief tells government forces to surrender.
newsitem.headline: Taleban chief tells government forces to surrender.

text.p: The leader of the Islamic Taleban rebels sweeping towards Kabul urged Afghan government forces on Wednesday to lay down their arms and surrender.
Mullah Mohammad Omar called on troops loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani to stop fighting because their leader was "preparing to flee," Omar's spokesman Wakil Ahmed said.
Omar said government security forces, such as police, should stay at their posts and guard markets and offices to prevent any looting that might take place after Kabul falls.
The Taleban said they were fighting government forces on the edge of Kabul on Wednesday after capturing the town of Sarobi, 70 km (44 miles) east of the capital, overnight.
"Whoever joins us can benefit from an amnesty," Ahmed, contacted at Taleban headquarters in the southern Afghan city of Kandahar, quoted Omar as saying.
The Taleban, who emerged from the obscurity of religious schools in Pakistan two years ago, have been fighting to oust Rabbani and impose a strict Islamic order across Afghanistan.
Omar said the Taleban had no ethnic or regional prejudices and had no desire to take revenge on anyone, but only wanted to enforce Islamic sharia (law) throughout the country.
